Control Parameters for islasso Fitting

Source: R/islasso.R
is.control.Rd

Collects the parameters controlling the fitting process of [islasso()] and [islasso.path()].

Usage

is.control(
  sigma2 = -1,
  tol = 1e-05,
  itmax = 1000,
  stand = TRUE,
  trace = 0,
  nfolds = 5,
  seed = NULL,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  g = 0.5,
  b0 = NULL,
  V0 = NULL,
  c = 0.5,
  inner = c("mm", "newton"),
  solver = c("auto", "dense", "woodbury"),
  ncores = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

sigma2

fixed value of the dispersion parameter; if negative (default) it is estimated (Pearson statistic over the residual degrees of freedom). Ignored for the binomial, Poisson and negative binomial families, where it is 1.

tol

tolerance of the convergence criteria (default `1e-5`).

itmax

maximum number of iterations (default 1000).

stand

logical: should the covariates be standardised (default `TRUE`)? With `stand = TRUE` the penalty acts on the standardised coefficients, as in glmnet; estimates are always returned on the original scale.

trace

integer: 0 (default) silent, 1 compact and 2 detailed printing of the iterations.

nfolds

number of folds for the cross-validation used when `lambda` is missing.

seed

optional integer seed for the cross-validation folds (the random number generator state of the session is restored afterwards).

adaptive

logical: adaptive lasso with weights based on the pseudo hat values (experimental).

g

numeric in \[0, 1\]: the parameter of the extended BIC (`g = 0` gives the BIC).

b0

optional starting values for the coefficients (original scale, intercept first).

V0

optional starting covariance matrix (or a number for its diagonal) on the standardised scale; default `0.01`.

c

the mixture weight of the induced smoothing (default 0.5), a number in \[0, 1\] or a vector with one value per coefficient; a negative value means that the weights are re-estimated at each iteration.

inner

the algorithm solving the smoothed estimating equation at fixed standard errors: `"mm"` (default, monotone majorise-minimise iterations, the undamped version of the fixed-point iterations of islasso 1.6) or `"newton"` (Newton's method with line search).

solver

linear algebra: `"auto"` (default) uses `"woodbury"` when the number of columns exceeds twice the number of observations and `"dense"` otherwise.

ncores

number of cores used by [islasso.path()] to fit the models for the different values of `lambda` in parallel (socket cluster of package 'parallel'); default 1.

...

further arguments, ignored (allows `do.call(is.control, control)`).

Value

A list with the control parameters.

See also

[islasso()], [islasso.path()]

Author

Gianluca Sottile gianluca.sottile@unipa.it

Examples

is.control(tol = 1e-6, seed = 1)
#> $sigma2
#> [1] -1
#> 
#> $tol
#> [1] 1e-06
#> 
#> $itmax
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $trace
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $stand
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $nfolds
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $adaptive
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $g
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $b0
#> NULL
#> 
#> $V0
#> NULL
#> 
#> $c
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $inner
#> [1] "mm"
#> 
#> $solver
#> [1] "auto"
#> 
#> $ncores
#> [1] 1
#>
